composio.note: Composio has no managed Spotify app, so you must register your own and give Composio its Client ID and Secret. Your own app starts in Development Mode: at most 5 Spotify users you allowlist by hand can connect, and the owner needs Premium. A Composio-hosted app would not lift these caps.

verdict.headline: You can connect yourself plus 4 hand-allowlisted users in about 30 minutes. Opening Spotify to the public requires a registered business with 250k+ MAU, a partner application and up to 6 weeks of review.
verdict.summary: Creating an app and doing OAuth is easy. Going beyond 5 users is effectively closed to new products: since May 15 2025, Spotify only grants extended quota to organizations (not individuals) with a launched service, 250k+ MAU and presence in key markets. Since Feb/Mar 2026, Development Mode apps also need the owner to have Premium and lose many endpoints. The Developer Policy also bans voice-assistant products that control Spotify and bans using Spotify content to train ML/AI models, which needs a careful read for an AI agent.
verdict.time_to_production: Not realistically reachable for a new product. If you already meet the criteria: partner application approval (unpublished time) plus a quota review of up to 6 weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1 hour for Development Mode. Several more hours for the partner application and quota questionnaire if you qualify.
verdict.approval_wait: Extended quota mode needs an approved Partner Application (company email required) and then a quota extension request. Spotify says review 'can take up to six weeks'. Development Mode has no review but caps you at 5 users.
verdict.cost: No API fee. The app owner must keep an active Spotify Premium subscription or Development Mode apps stop working.

phases.name: Register the app
phases.goal: Have a Development Mode app with Client ID and Secret

steps.title: Use a Spotify account with active Premium
steps.detail: Since Feb 11 2026 for new apps (and Mar 9 2026 for existing ones), every Development Mode app needs its owner to have an active Premium subscription. If it lapses, the app stops working until the owner resubscribes. Use a team-owned account.

steps.title: Create the app and accept the Developer Terms
steps.detail: In the Dashboard, click Create an App and enter the App Name and App Description, which users see on the consent screen. Tick the Developer Terms of Service and click Create. The name must not start with 'Spot' or be confusable with Spotify.
steps.agent_help: Draft the app name and description and check the name against the Developer Policy branding rules.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Both are on the app overview page. If the secret may be exposed, click ROTATE.
steps.agent_help: Prepare env var names (SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID, SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET) so the secret never goes into chat.

phases.name: Configure redirect URIs
phases.goal: Have redirect URIs that pass Spotify's validation

steps.title: Add the Composio callback and a loopback dev URI
steps.detail: Under Edit Settings, add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback and the website URL. For local development use http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback or http://[::1]:PORT/callback. 'localhost' is not allowed, and plain http is only allowed for loopback IP literals. Matching is exact, with one exception: loopback IPs may omit the port to allow a dynamic one.
steps.agent_help: Generate the exact URI strings and check them against Spotify's rules and the redirect_uri Composio sends. You paste and save them.

phases.name: Connect to Composio
phases.goal: Have your own Spotify account connected through your app via Composio

steps.title: Create a custom auth config for SPOTIFY in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, choose Spotify, and select OAuth2. Paste the Client ID and Secret and click Create, then pass the auth config ID in your session's authConfigs. Register the redirect URI the dashboard shows, normally https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Some toolkits still default to the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, so copy whichever URI is displayed.
steps.agent_help: Create the auth config through the Composio API or SDK from env vars and verify the redirect URI matches the Spotify app setting exactly.

steps.title: Pick minimal scopes
steps.detail: Request only what the agent needs, for example user-read-private user-read-email playlist-read-private playlist-modify-private user-library-read user-read-playback-state user-modify-playback-state. Spotify's policy says to request and process only the data needed to run your app.
steps.agent_help: Map each agent tool to its required scope and set the scope list on the auth config.

steps.title: Connect your own account and smoke-test
steps.detail: Approve consent, then call GET /me and one action endpoint. Avoid endpoints removed for Development Mode, such as batch GET /tracks, /browse/new-releases, /artists/{id}/top-tracks and GET /users/{id}. Search is capped at limit=10.
steps.agent_help: Run the test calls after you approve, and report which agent tools hit removed or restricted endpoints so they can be rewritten (for example, fetch tracks one ID at a time).

phases.name: Run in Development Mode (up to 5 users)
phases.goal: Have up to 5 known testers connect

steps.title: Allowlist each tester
steps.detail: Under Settings > Users Management, click Add new user and enter the tester's name and Spotify account email. Up to 5 users can use a Development Mode app. Users who are not allowlisted get HTTP 403 on API calls even if login appears to succeed.
steps.agent_help: Collect testers' Spotify account emails into a checklist. Community reports say the allowlist cannot be automated.

phases.name: Apply for extended quota mode
phases.goal: Have the app approved to be installed by unlimited users
phases.duration: Up to 6 weeks of review after partner approval

steps.title: Check eligibility honestly
steps.detail: Spotify requires a legally registered business or organisation, an active launched service, at least 250k MAU, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability and adherence to the Terms. Individuals cannot apply (since May 15 2025). Spotify says over 95% of past applications fell short of basic security, privacy and licensing standards.
steps.agent_help: Score your product against each criterion and the Developer Policy, including the bans on voice-assistant control, ML/AI training and business-targeted products. Write a go/no-go memo.

steps.title: Submit the Partner Application from a company email
steps.detail: Submit the Partner Application form linked from the quota modes page. It must come from a company email address.
steps.agent_help: Draft answers (business details, MAU evidence, market availability, data handling) for you to review and submit.

steps.title: Request the quota extension in the Dashboard
steps.detail: After the partner form is approved, open the app, go to Settings > Quota extension Request, complete the 4-step questionnaire and click Submit.
steps.agent_help: Pre-draft the questionnaire answers and a screen-by-screen description of how Spotify data and branding appear in your product.

steps.title: Wait for Spotify's review
steps.detail: Spotify says 'This review process can take up to six weeks.' Extra quota applies only to the use case Spotify reviewed, and access can be revoked for policy violations.

requirements.item: Active Spotify Premium subscription on the app owner's account
requirements.detail: Required for every Development Mode app since Feb 11 2026 (new apps) and Mar 9 2026 (existing apps).
Ticked when you create the app.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URI, or a loopback IP literal for local development
requirements.detail: 'localhost' is rejected. Enforced for new apps since Apr 9 2025, with all clients expected to migrate by Nov 2025.

requirements.item: Allowlisted users (name and Spotify email), maximum 5

requirements.detail: Extended quota applications are accepted only from organizations, not individuals, since May 15 2025.

requirements.item: Launched service with at least 250k MAU in key Spotify markets
requirements.detail: Listed implementation requirements for extended quota mode, alongside commercial viability and adherence to the Terms.

requirements.item: Approved Partner Application submitted from a company email
requirements.detail: Must be approved before the in-Dashboard quota extension request.

scopes.purpose: Identify the user (GET /me), country and subscription level, and email
scopes.review_impact: No per-scope review. All scopes are limited by the app's quota mode.

scopes.purpose: List and read the user's playlists
scopes.review_impact: No per-scope review. In Development Mode, playlist items can only be read for playlists the user owns or collaborates on.

scopes.purpose: Create playlists and add or remove items
scopes.review_impact: No per-scope review. POST /users/{user_id}/playlists is removed in Development Mode; use the /me equivalents.

scopes.purpose: Read and save items in the user's library
scopes.review_impact: No per-scope review. Development Mode apps must use PUT/DELETE /me/library with Spotify URIs.

scopes.purpose: See what is playing and control playback
scopes.review_impact: No per-scope review, but the Developer Policy prohibits voice-control or voice-assistant products that control Spotify. Check this before building conversational playback control.
No per-scope review, but the policy bans analyzing Spotify content to build user profiles and bans using it to train ML/AI models.

oauth.pkce: Supported (S256). Recommended when the secret cannot be stored safely; the PKCE token request sends client_id and code_verifier with no secret. The confidential Authorization Code flow, used by Composio, sends Basic base64(client_id:client_secret).
oauth.refresh_tokens: Returned by the Authorization Code and PKCE flows. Access tokens last 1 hour. A refresh may or may not return a new refresh_token; keep the old one if none is returned. Refresh tokens last 6 months from user authorization, and refreshing does not extend them. After that, invalid_grant is returned and the user must re-authorize.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must exactly match a registered URI, including case and trailing slashes. HTTPS is required except for loopback IP literals (http://127.0.0.1:PORT, http://[::1]:PORT). 'localhost' is not allowed. Dynamic ports are allowed only for loopback IPs registered without a port. Enforced for new apps since Apr 9 2025.

limits.limit: At most 5 authenticated users per Development Mode app
limits.applies_when: All apps not in extended quota mode (existing apps with more users keep them)
limits.how_to_lift: Extended quota mode: approved partner application plus quota request (org, 250k+ MAU)

limits.limit: Development Mode endpoint removals: batch GETs (/tracks, /albums, /artists and others), /browse/new-releases, /browse/categories, /artists/{id}/top-tracks, GET /users/{id} and others; search limit at most 10
limits.applies_when: Development Mode apps since Feb 11 2026 (new) and Mar 9 2026 (existing)
limits.how_to_lift: Extended quota mode apps are unaffected

limits.limit: Restricted endpoints: Recommendations, Related Artists, Audio Features, Audio Analysis, Featured and Category playlists, preview URLs in multi-get, algorithmic and editorial playlists
limits.applies_when: Apps registered on or after Nov 27 2024, and Development Mode apps without a pending extension at that date
limits.how_to_lift: No lift documented. Only apps that already had extended access are unaffected.

limits.limit: Rate limit over a rolling 30-second window (no number published); HTTP 429 with Retry-After
limits.applies_when: All apps. Development Mode's limit is lower than extended quota's.
limits.how_to_lift: Honor Retry-After. Extended quota mode has a 'much higher' limit.

limits.limit: Refresh tokens expire 6 months after authorization
limits.applies_when: All apps registered in the Developer Dashboard
limits.how_to_lift: Cannot be lifted. Prompt users to re-authorize before expiry.

blockers.symptom: The user can log in, but API calls with their token return HTTP 403
blockers.fix: Add them under Settings > Users Management (5 max) or obtain extended quota

blockers.symptom: You cannot save 'http://localhost:...' or a non-loopback http URI, or authorize fails because redirect_uri does not match exactly
blockers.fix: Use https (the Composio callback) or http://127.0.0.1:PORT, and match the registered string exactly

blockers.symptom: The Development Mode app stops working for everyone
blockers.fix: Resubscribe the owner account to Premium

blockers.blocker: Agent calls a removed or restricted endpoint
blockers.symptom: Calls to recommendations, audio-features, batch /tracks, /artists/{id}/top-tracks and similar endpoints fail for a new or Development Mode app
blockers.fix: Rewrite tools to use single-ID fetches, /me endpoints and /me/library. Recommendation-style features have no replacement.
Discard the token and re-run authorization. Track the grant date and prompt re-consent early.

blockers.symptom: The partner application or quota request is declined (individual developer, under 250k MAU, or use case not aligned)
blockers.fix: None for a new product. Keep Spotify as a 5-user personal feature, or reassess once the business meets the criteria.

agent_can: Draft the app name and description and check them against the branding rules
Generate valid redirect URIs (Composio https callback, 127.0.0.1 loopback) and verify exact match
Create the Composio SPOTIFY auth config via API and set minimal scopes
Smoke-test after you consent and flag tools that hit removed or restricted Development Mode endpoints
Assess extended-quota eligibility and policy risks (voice-assistant control, AI/ML training ban) in a go/no-go memo
Pre-draft the Partner Application and 4-step quota questionnaire answers
you_must: Own the app on a Spotify account with active Premium
Create the app and accept the Developer Terms
Copy and store the Client ID and Secret
Approve the consent screen for your own test connection
Manually add each of up to 5 testers by name and Spotify email
Submit the Partner Application from a company email and the quota request, representing a registered business

uncertain: Spotify does not publish how long Partner Application approval takes. Only the quota review's 'up to six weeks' is stated, so total time to production is unknown.

Whether an AI agent that controls playback counts as a prohibited 'voice-control or voice-assistant' product (Policy III.3) is an interpretation. A text-based agent may differ from a voice one. Get legal review.
Whether a hosted AI agent product counts as 'targeted at businesses' or as commercial use of a streaming SDA under the Developer Policy is not addressed directly.
Rate-limit numbers are not published, only that Development Mode's limit is lower.
The claim that the 5-user allowlist cannot be automated comes from community forum search snippets; no official page says so either way.
Older Spotify material (a 2021 blog and forum posts) cites a 25-user Development Mode cap. Current docs say 5; existing apps that already had more users keep them.
The exact error shown for a non-allowlisted user at consent time (versus the documented 403 on API calls) was not verified.
Time estimates for Development Mode setup are hands-on estimates, not provider SLAs.
